races.name: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Now Maiden Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Firebrand
runners_data.note: Solid recent placed form on Good ground over 16-18f, runs prominently and handles this trip well; six-year-old consistency is a plus but has yet to win in 15 similar-going runs, which is a concern at any price.

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with just one hurdles start in this form column, runs prominently but has shown limited placed form on Good ground (0/3 placed in 15 similar-going runs); short layoff of 13 days is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Strong profile for this race — six placed efforts from 11 similar-going runs suggests consistency, and Andrew Slattery's yard is in good form (7/25 in 14 days); the R and U in the form string signal jumping lapses that must not recur.

runners_data.name: First Ascent
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained prominent runner with five placed finishes from nine Good-ground starts; headgear (tongue-tie/pads) suggests connections are managing him carefully, and a 13-day turnaround implies he is ready.

runners_data.name: Geashill Poet
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed — no form string, no historical run data, unknown going preference; style tagged UNKNOWN and yard (0/1 in 14 days) gives no confidence angle, making this horse a pure gamble.

runners_data.name: Man Down
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a fading finish pattern and only one recorded run on Good ground (finishing 10th); style UNKNOWN with a fade flag, which is a significant negative in a maiden where the tempo is likely to expose weaknesses late.

runners_data.name: Midfield Magic
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, returning after 151 days off; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) tempers confidence in how effectively this horse will control the race, and the long break adds uncertainty despite Gavin Cromwell's solid 14-day record.

runners_data.name: Scotty Joe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won from off the pace (form includes a "1" at 16f on Good ground); 89-day layoff is notable but J J Slevin-calibre rider Shane O'Callaghan (3) brings some positional awareness for this wait-and-pounce style.

runners_data.name: Tomthescaffolder
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride for Henry De Bromhead — a strong jockey-trainer pairing — and this hold-up performer has four placed finishes from five Good-ground runs; tongue-tie and pads suggest a horse that needs careful handling.

runners_data.name: Blue Johnl
runners_data.note: Fades in finish pattern is flagged and two Good-ground runs produced finishes of 8th and 9th; J J Slevin is a top booking but the form string (P-R498) includes a refusal and a fall, making reliability a live concern.

runners_data.name: Down After Dark
runners_data.note: Just one run (unseated) and very fresh at 6 days since last out; style UNKNOWN but hood headgear suggests a horse that needs settling, and the S Curling yard's 1/11 14-day record offers slim trainer confidence.

runners_data.name: Power Of Knowledge
runners_data.note: W P Mullins sends out a four-year-old with one run (5th on Good ground) and retains Mark Walsh — that combination in a maiden of this level commands respect regardless of the sparse form; clearly holds unexposed upside.

runners_data.name: Bayswater Bloom
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying the lightest weight (151lbs) and consistent Good-ground form (four runs, all 5th-10th); Miss Evanna McCutcheon's yard is 0/1 in 14 days and this horse has yet to place, but the patient style suits a late-run scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Midfield Magic is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner maiden hurdle, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) suggests this horse is operating somewhat out of natural role and should not be taken as a dominant, class-assured pace-setter. Behind Midfield Magic, a cluster of prominent-style runners — Firebrand, Baila Conmigo, Whats New, and First Ascent — will press forward and contest early positions, meaning the early gallop on Good ground at Kilbeggan should be honest but not frantic, with no single horse able to dictate in isolation. With Midfield Magic unlikely to face serious front-running pressure from a genuine rival, the pace should be sustainable and even, setting up a race where stamina and jumping fluency through the latter stages become the decisive factors. This shape — a controlled, single-pacemaker tempo on Good ground over 2m — most favours hold-up horses and strong travellers who can pick off the prominent runners in the straight, with Scotty Joe, Tomthescaffolder, and Bayswater Bloom potentially best placed to benefit if their finishing kicks are ignited.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Midfield Magic sets a sustainable tempo unchallenged and the prominent runners tire in the straight, allowing closers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: The honest but undemanding gallop set by Midfield Magic keeps the prominent runners within their comfort zone until the final flight, where stamina separates the field; hold-up horses with proven Good-ground form can pick off fading front-runners. Scotty Joe's win from off the pace suits this shape, and Tomthescaffolder's consistent placed efforts in similar conditions make both attractive profiles here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves moderate enough that prominent types conserve energy and kick clear before closers can mount a challenge.
scenarios.body: Firebrand and Whats New have strong recent form running prominently on Good ground, and both carry the placed consistency to sustain their efforts into the final stages of a 2m hurdle at Kilbeggan; a genuinely slow early tempo plays directly into their hands. First Ascent's course experience and prominent style also keeps this horse relevant in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced unexposed horses — Power Of Knowledge, Down After Dark, or Geashill Poet — produces a performance well above their limited public form.
scenarios.body: W P Mullins's Power Of Knowledge carries the pedigree and yard quality to be significantly better than a single run suggests, and Good ground over 2m is an entirely plausible debut context for improvement; a field of maidens with modest ORs increases the chance an unexposed type lands a surprise. Down After Dark's handling of Good ground and the Curling yard's quiet confidence could also trigger this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Errors Cost Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors from prominent types disrupt the race shape and gift a fortuitous winner from further back.
scenarios.body: Kilbeggan's tight, undulating track catches out inexperienced jumpers, and with several young or lightly raced horses pressing forward early, a faller or unseater in front could create chaotic, strung-out running; a hold-up horse unaffected by early drama would inherit a clear run. Bayswater Bloom's patient tactics and Scotty Joe's rearward positioning mean both avoid the worst of any front-end carnage.

watchPoints.text: Midfield Magic's 151-day absence combined with the STYLE_FIT flag means the pace-setting role could collapse mid-race — watch for this horse stopping quickly after the second last, which would dramatically reshape the finish.

Whats New has an "R" (refused) and "U" (unseated) in recent form; if this horse makes a jumping error at Kilbeggan's tight hurdles, it risks taking out other prominent runners and distorting the race for the whole field.

Blue Johnl's form string includes a refusal and a fall, and a fading-finish flag adds to the concern — J J Slevin needs to nurse this horse into the race, but any early jumping drama could turn a manageable issue into a dangerous incident.

Power Of Knowledge (Mullins/Mark Walsh) and Down After Dark (Curling/Enright) are both unexposed four-year-olds whose market moves at the off should be tracked — any significant support into the field would signal stable confidence not visible in the form.

Scotty Joe has not run for 89 days — if the horse travels strongly early under Shane O'Callaghan, that is a positive fitness signal; if the horse is pushed along before the home turn, the layoff has left its mark.

races.name: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Now Maiden Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Bud Fox
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing five-year-old trained by Gavin Cromwell whose win and place form on Good ground (3 from 5 in similar conditions) makes this track and surface a strong fit; 117 days off but Cromwell's yard is in decent form at 4/39 over 14 days, and the hood worn previously is a focus aid that suits sharp Kilbeggan.

runners_data.name: Combs
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Gordon Elliott fitted with a tongue-tie, who has shown consistent placed form on Good ground and sets the early pace here; the key question is whether a genuinely contested lead against Texas Red blunts him before the finish, but at 150 days off he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Goeasyonme
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old — just one run, a second on Soft — whose unknown ceiling is the main angle; trainer John Patrick Ryan has a quiet recent book (0/18 in 14 days) but this horse's single run suggests a horse that tracks the pace and this Good surface removes the Soft query.

runners_data.name: Jack Spriggins
runners_data.note: Off the track for a remarkable 748 days and with a flat-racing background over short trips, the step to hurdles over 2m is a major unknown; hold-up style suits a run-to-learn scenario rather than a winning return, and the 7lb claimer is notable.

runners_data.name: Joly Saphir
runners_data.note: Returned an eighth on Good ground over 2m4f last time and carries the "fades in finish" flag; natural hold-up horse for Philip Fenton whose one similar-going run produced nothing, and who needs a very fast pace to have any hope of landing a blow from the rear.

runners_data.name: Texas Red
runners_data.note: Second front-runner who will press Combs for the lead, shaped by P J Rothwell and active recently (24 days since last run); has shown consistent placed form at 2m on Good ground but his record of 0W1P from seven similar-going starts suggests he tends to be galloped into the ground rather than winning outright.

runners_data.name: Unfortunatecharlie
runners_data.note: Unknown going profile (flagged UNKNOWN) but placed form of 2/1 in bumpers hints at ability; lightly raced seven-year-old for Noel Kelly whose style (unclassified) and 124-day absence create real uncertainty, though bumper form of 2nd and 1st suggests a horse capable of finishing close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Lucky Signal
runners_data.note: Elliott-trained four-year-old who faded on both hurdle starts including a course run on Good; the "fades in finish" flag and a pulled-up run in the form string are red lights, and from a hold-up position this race shape doesn't offer what this horse needs.

runners_data.name: Mydreamtell
runners_data.note: Two runs on Good — an eighth and a sixth — from an unclassified running style suggest a horse finding its feet over hurdles; trainer James Fahey has no runners in the 14-day window and the form string offers no encouragement for a first-time win.

runners_data.name: Telegram Sam
runners_data.note: Sole comparable Good-ground run produced a fourth and the P in the form string raises jumping questions; unclassified style for Adrian Murray (0/1 in 14 days) and 101 days off — a lightly raced unknown who needs everything to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Inver Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent placings on Good ground are the best thing on his CV, but this seven-year-old's natural come-from-behind style is squeezed into a midfield berth here because of the cluster of hold-up horses in the field — racing out of his preferred role markedly diminishes what his finishing kick can deliver.

runners_data.name: Jukebox Jolene
runners_data.note: Two runs on Good ground produced a seventh and an eighth, and though the hold-up style could theoretically suit a strongly run race, there is nothing in the form to suggest the ability to take advantage; Tom Dreaper's yard is quiet (0/1 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Asthelightdeclines
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second string here has a form string of B77 and a last-time-out dash after a break; a true hold-up runner forced into a midfield role by the density of hold-up horses in this field, which blunts any chance of producing a decisive late effort from his preferred deep position.

runners_data.name: Cahir Bay
runners_data.note: Youngest of the hold-up contingent with Flat experience over shorter trips and a form debut showing a 14th and a 6th — raw profile for M Flannery; naturally wants to come from off the pace but will be unable to secure that position comfortably, making the redistribution into midfield a significant structural disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Combs and Texas Red are the two confirmed front-runners in this 14-runner maiden hurdle, and with both likely to press for the early lead, this race will be run at an honest, contested gallop from the off rather than drifting into a falsely run affair. That genuine pace on Good ground over 2m at Kilbeggan — a sharp, flat track that naturally suits those who can travel prominently — creates a race shape where staying close to the action matters enormously. Bud Fox is the obvious beneficiary from the prominent group, able to sit just off the pace-setters and pounce, while true hold-up horses face a stiffer task closing from the rear against a fast-run tempo. The field holds more hold-up types than the track map can accommodate at the rear — Inver Bay, Cahir Bay, and Asthelightdeclines are genuine come-from-behind horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield rather than their natural position, diluting their effectiveness. On balance, this race shape strongly favours prominent or close-tracking runners who can control their own destiny without relying on a tactical injection of late pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Combs and Texas Red fight it out up front and the pace stays honest, allowing a close-tracking prominent horse to cruise into contention before the last.
scenarios.body: Bud Fox is perfectly positioned to exploit this shape, having won on Good ground at this sort of trip and wearing headgear (hood) to sharpen focus; Combs, despite setting the pace, could have enough in reserve to hold on if the early fractions don't overly drain him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders — most likely Combs — gets a soft lead when the other fades early, allowing a solo dictator to set a controlled tempo and steal a march.
scenarios.body: Combs, trained by Gordon Elliott and fitted with a hood, has the profile to control proceedings if Texas Red capitulates through lack of stamina at this 2m trip on Good; a horse that leads with cover from the chasing group is very hard to peg back around Kilbeggan's flat, sharp circuit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to burn out both leaders and a horse racing just off midfield finds a clear run from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Goeasyonme — lightly raced, showing a second on hurdle debut — could improve markedly for that experience, while Unfortunatecharlie carries some unexposed form that leaves room for a bold display from this position; both need the leaders to do each other damage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a truly scorching pace and the race develops into a stamina test where late finishers from further back mop up.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely scenario given the redistribution of Inver Bay, Cahir Bay, and Asthelightdeclines into midfield rather than their preferred deep hold-up berths, meaning none will be producing their optimum run; Jukebox Jolene or Joly Saphir could be beneficiaries but only if the pace is genuinely destructive, which is improbable on Good ground.

watchPoints.text: Combs and Texas Red — watch the opening half-mile to see which horse blinks first in the pace duel; if Texas Red is pushed wide or folds before the halfway mark, Combs gets a soft lead that transforms his winning chance significantly.

Bud Fox — track his position at the first two flights; if Donoghue settles him directly behind the two leaders in a clear second rank, he is in the race-winning position and punters should treat him as a serious threat from that point.

Inver Bay, Cahir Bay, Asthelightdeclines — all three are natural hold-up horses crammed into a busy rear-midfield group; watch whether any of them are blocked for a run turning for home, as a lack of daylight at a crucial point would effectively end their chances before the last.

Goeasyonme — lightly raced with a single run and an unclassified map position; watch the market moves in the final 30 minutes before the off, as stable confidence from the Ryan yard on a horse with a big unknown ceiling could be a significant pointer.

Jack Spriggins — 748 days off the track and dropping in trip compared to Flat form; watch his jumping at the early flights, as any novice error could compromise his race and signal this is purely a learning run rather than a live winning attempt.

races.name: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction & Median Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Coral Reid
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Tom Kelly claiming, needs a genuinely strong gallop to close from the rear; the controlled pace Rokanako is likely to set is a concern, and with only one run to go on (seventh at Sligo on soft) her profile is almost entirely unknown.

runners_data.name: Eternal Reward
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins partners a mare who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish across her three hurdle starts, and a history of two pulled-ups and a fall over hurdles underlines the stamina question over 2m3f Good — the similar-going record of zero wins, zero places is telling.

runners_data.name: It's All Clear
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse with five consecutive top-four finishes on Good ground at 16-20f for Mrs Cashin, and the tongue-tie application suggests connections are looking for a small edge; travels prominently and has the course-distance profile to be competitive here.

runners_data.name: Rokanako
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Edward Power who has the pace to dictate on Good ground and won over 2m on similar going last time; style_fit of 0.93 notes he is technically labelled prominent but he is functioning as the lone pace-setter, which is entirely in his favour in a race that has no one to push him.

runners_data.name: Splendid Fellow
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's five-year-old returns after a 115-day break but brings the strongest placed form in the race, including seconds at 2m4f Good and 2m1f Yielding; a prominent runner who jumped fluently in those efforts, and the class and jumping ability could prove decisive if he returns fit.

runners_data.name: Bigcitydreams
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's lightly raced gelding has only one hurdle start on record (pulled up) and missed 334 days between runs — Jordan Gainford takes the ride but there is simply insufficient evidence to assess style or ability with confidence; 7lb weight advantage over rivals is the one objective factor.

runners_data.name: Western Shores
runners_data.note: Has finished in the 5-6 range across all four hurdle starts on Good and similar going for Elliott; a genuine hold-up horse whose position on the map is forward of his natural running style — his true closer's profile is structurally disadvantaged by the uncontested pace Rokanako will set.

runners_data.name: La Muleta
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a single run to her name (second on hurdle debut for Rothwell) carrying 157lbs as the lightest in the field; Kevin Healy claims 7lbs but her style and ability over this extra trip are unknown, making her a wild card whose probability of winning rests entirely on untapped improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Rokanako is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger willing to contest the lead at 2m3f on Good ground, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop from flag to finish. Splendid Fellow and It's All Clear will press forward into prominent positions just behind, creating a compact early order that is unlikely to be frantic or strung out. The field does hold more hold-up types than a small field of eight can truly accommodate — Western Shores is a genuine hold-up horse shuffled forward on the map, and with Rokanako setting a measured pace, the rear-guard will need to close an honest but not punishing gap from the home turn. This race shape — a controlled single-paced gallop from one clear front-runner — strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield finisher who travels well and can sustain a clean jumping effort over the final three hurdles, rather than a pure closer who needs a truly searching gallop to get home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rokanako Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rokanako jumps fluently, dictates a genuine but uncontested pace and Splendid Fellow or It's All Clear track without applying pressure.
scenarios.body: Rokanako sets fractions that suit himself and a well-travelling prominent racer, and the field closes on a rhythm rather than a sprint — horses that jump well and travel handy into the straight have all the advantages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If Splendid Fellow or It's All Clear press Rokanako hard enough to set up a genuine test and the front two tire in the straight.
scenarios.body: A contested pace from the front elevates the contest into an stamina examination over the final two hurdles, lifting the chance of a prominent horse who was sitting just off the pace with cover.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Bigcitydreams or La Muleta, both lightly raced unknowns, prove substantially better than their sparse form suggests and travel powerfully through the race.
scenarios.body: Either newcomer could hold unexposed ability that renders form ratings meaningless; a well-judged ride from a confident pilot could see them emerge late from midfield as the front two exhaust each other.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely end-to-end and the prominent horses all tire, leaving the hold-up horses with ground to make up but a weakening target.
scenarios.body: Western Shores is mapped to midfield but is a true hold-up horse whose style_fit is compromised by the race shape; Coral Reid and Eternal Reward are the truest closers but need a strong pace that this uncontested leader is unlikely to set.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rokanako at the first two hurdles — if he flusters or loses his rhythm early, the pace structure collapses and the race becomes far more tactical, opening it up to prominent rivals like Splendid Fellow.

Eternal Reward's tendency to fade in the finish is a red flag at 2m3f; if she is held up and asks for a late effort, Danny Mullins should be watched to see whether she responds or drops away from the second-last.

Bigcitydreams has 334 days between runs and only one hurdle start ending in a pull-up — watch her body language in the preliminaries and early in the race for any sign she is not ready to produce a competitive effort.

Western Shores is mapped to midfield but is a true hold-up horse; watch whether Danny Gilligan actively holds him back from his shown position — if he does, the redistribution is confirmed and his chance diminishes further in a controlled-pace scenario.

La Muleta is stepping up significantly in trip on just one run; watch her jumping fluency — any hesitation or novice errors at hurdles will cost her lengths she cannot afford to concede on this course configuration at 2m3f.

races.name: Midland Breeders Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tir Og
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for E Seymour, Good ground is fine (sim-going record solid), but 81 days off and a habit of fading in recent form (38-704) raises questions about sustaining the gallop over 2m3f in a pace battle.

runners_data.name: Ivana D'alco
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins runner for Brian Hayes, won last time on Good ground over 21f and is fresh at 28 days; the other confirmed front-runner, hood fitted, and holds the best recent form of the two pace-setters — most likely to benefit if the duel breaks her rival.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Returned just six days ago and has a warning flag for fading late; holds a Good-ground win on the profile but the quick turnaround and tendency to empty at the finish makes the trip a genuine concern in a truly-run 2m3f.

runners_data.name: Del Boys Diva
runners_data.note: Won two of last three on Good ground over shorter, tongue-tie fitted, and Keith Donoghue booked — a fader flag is present but two recent course victories suggest she finds more than the data implies when fresh; the step up to 2m3f is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Shirzan
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with limited hurdles experience but a win on Soft and placed runs at 16f — natural hold-up type who has only once run on this type of Good/Firm ground profile at this trip; a young, unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Diamond Tipp
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap and cheekpieces fitted, Sean Flanagan takes the ride; placed at 18f on Good recently and trainer has a 1/5 strike rate over 14 days — consistent placed horse who stays well but has not won since early in career.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Ciaran Murphy who has been in fine form (2/15 T14), ran just eight days ago and placed at 20f on Good — natural position just off the leaders makes this trip ideal, and recent run fitness is an asset in an 18-runner field.

runners_data.name: Laurie Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare for E D Delany, 55 days off and a pulled-up run last time out; tongue-tie worn, patchy form at this level, and the layoff combined with the big field makes it hard to be positive.

runners_data.name: Andyourbirdcansing
runners_data.note: Prominent type for John Patrick Ryan whose T14 record (0/18) is a significant negative flag; won at 20f on Good in good style but form has gone cold since, and the trainer's current run rate is a concern.

runners_data.name: Bowgate Street
runners_data.note: Useful performer on Good ground at around 18-19f, tongue-tie fitted — a genuine hold-up horse whose natural style is to race from the rear, but the volume of hold-up types in this field means he may find himself racing closer than ideal; STYLE_FIT 0.94 tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Evelyn
runners_data.note: Good-ground record is limited (0W1P on similar going) and she has not run since 55 days ago; this mare's instinct is to race from the back, but the compressed field means she will likely be positioned further forward than she wants — STYLE_FIT 0.93.

runners_data.name: Last Note
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort at 20f on Good back in the form, but 90 days off is a concern; hunts from the rear by nature and in a race with this many hold-up horses, getting a clear run late from her natural position will be very difficult — STYLE_FIT 0.92.

runners_data.name: Circus Act
runners_data.note: Has blinkers and tongue-tie, showed a fourth at 14f on Soft suggesting she handles pace changes — another true closer whose redistribution into midfield reflects the field's makeup; ran 41 days ago and lacks the class to offset positional compromise — STYLE_FIT 0.92.

runners_data.name: Chemdawg
runners_data.note: Placed twice on Soft at 19-22f and won on Good at 19f — genuine form over the trip, blinkers and tongue-tie fitted, 24 days since last run; a legitimate hold-up horse with staying credentials, but mapped forward of her natural ground and the STYLE_FIT 0.93 flag limits optimism.

runners_data.name: Larkins Lane
runners_data.note: Won twice at 20f on Good and Soft, P J Rothwell's yard is in form (T14: 4/21), ran 27 days ago — she is the most interesting of the redistributed hold-up types because her actual form over this trip on this going is strong; cheekpieces fitted and could get closer to the pace than her natural style suggests.

runners_data.name: Demanding Gerry
runners_data.note: Multiple placed runs at 17-20f on Good, amateur rider Shane O'Callaghan (3), tongue-tie worn, 41 days off — consistent stayer but without a win in this form string; true hold-up horse positioned forward of preference, and the claim may not be enough to offset the style disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Frontier Rose
runners_data.note: Fades-in-finish flag, no jockey listed, never won on Good ground, form string (0-0866) is consistently moderate — a redistributed hold-up type with no obvious route to the frame in this competitive mares' handicap.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: 337 days since last run is a massive concern regardless of form; fades late, no jockey declared, and the redistribution means she will not get her natural position off the pace — returning from near a year off in an 18-runner field is a very tough ask.

races.paceDynamic: Tir Og and Ivana D'alco are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over 2m3f at Kilbeggan, creating a genuinely contested gallop on Good ground that is unlikely to suit either of them to dominate unchallenged. Steps In The Sand and Andyourbirdcansing add prominent pace further back, meaning the tempo should be honest and sustained throughout, compressing the field and making it harder for any lone leader to dictate. The redistribution note is critical here: Bowgate Street, Evelyn, Last Note, Circus Act, Chemdawg, Larkins Lane, Demanding Gerry, Frontier Rose and St Anthonys Corner are all natural hold-up types shuffled into the midfield map because there is simply not enough room at the rear — of those, Larkins Lane and Bowgate Street are the most likely to actually secure a position closer to the pace than their label suggests. With a genuine pace battle up front and a big, open field of 18, this race shape strongly favours a prominent-to-midfield racer with stamina who can travel into a fast-run race and pick off the leaders as they tire in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Battle, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tir Og and Ivana D'alco push each other along at a genuine clip and the leaders empty inside the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: The contested front-running duel drains both pace-setters, and a prominent-tracking horse with superior stamina swoops to claim a weakening leader; Good ground suits smooth travellers at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Ivana D'alco (or Tir Og) gains a slight tactical advantage early and is able to dictate a controlled tempo despite the other's presence.
scenarios.body: One of the two front-runners edges ahead and controls the race sufficiently that Brian Hayes on Ivana D'alco, with the Mullins formbook and recent Good-ground win, gets first run at the final flight; the other front-runner fades having done too much work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Ranker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, allowing a well-handicapped midfield type to pick off tired rivals in the straight.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting fourth to sixth early, tracking the battle without expending energy, arrives with a run when the front two crack; Small Bucks and Del Boys Diva both carry hold-up flags but have winning course-and-distance profiles that suit a strong-run 2m3f.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is extreme and the entire prominent group wilts, handing an advantage to a true back-marker arriving from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses like Bowgate Street or Last Note racing from their natural deep position, but both are mapped out of role in this field, significantly undermining the likelihood of a true late flourish; only if the race falls apart completely does a closer benefit.

watchPoints.text: Tir Og and Ivana D'alco will set the pace together — watch which one is travelling more easily after the third hurdle, as the one that folds first could trigger a significant market move in running.

Larkins Lane (Rothwell, T14: 4/21) is the most likely beneficiary among the redistributed hold-up types — if she gets an opening on the inside after the last bend she could appear from an unexpected position.

Steps In The Sand ran just eight days ago — watch her behaviour in the paddock and whether Eoin Walsh can hold a prominent position cleanly at the start with 18 runners breaking; a scrimmage could cost her the race before it begins.

Several runners (Frontier Rose, St Anthonys Corner, Circus Act) carry fades-in-finish flags or long layoffs and may cause interference in the home straight as they weaken — punters on hold-up horses should note the traffic risk.

The Mullins booking of Brian Hayes for Ivana D'alco (T14: 4/26) stands out as the strongest trainer-jockey combination in the race — monitor whether she drifts or firms in the market as a proxy for stable confidence.

races.name: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hey Sir
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist whose recent form string reads poorly (6-3764), and his last five runs on similar ground show no wins and no places; J J Slevin is a quality booking, but the horse's finishing pattern shows limited improvement from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Kingston Silver
runners_data.note: True back-of-field type by style, flagged for fading in the finish, who has only one run on record (12th at 2m Good); placed in midfield by the mapping because of the crowded hold-up population, which further disadvantages his chance.

runners_data.name: Tell Me See
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose three runs on similar going all produced mid-pack finishes; the fading-in-finish flag compounds an already modest profile, and Eoin Walsh has limited room to manoeuvre on a horse who has never threatened a podium place.

runners_data.name: The Bossman About
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed six-year-old with no public form or going preference recorded; Carl Millar (5) claiming reduces the weight burden slightly, but the absence of any data makes meaningful assessment impossible.

runners_data.name: Through The Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who finds Good ground more familiar than soft, though all three career starts have come at shorter trips; Philip Donovan rides for a trainer in solid 14-day form (3/12) and a forward position looks achievable in this pace context.

runners_data.name: Not In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a single run to his name — a placed effort at 2m on Good — who is a natural hold-up horse by style, though the compressed pace map means he is likely to find himself in midfield rather than off the true back; Simon Torrens takes the ride for a trainer with a recent winner.

runners_data.name: Blue Trix
runners_data.note: Unraced under rules on any going, so style and ceiling are genuinely unknown; Danny Mullins and W P Mullins (4/26 last 14 days) give this debutante serious stable and jockey credentials that cannot be dismissed despite the data void.

runners_data.name: Online Order
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by inclination, wearing hood and tongue-tie, whose last three runs place him 8th, 6th and 7th; pushed into the midfield map by the congestion of closers, he is racing further out of his natural role and his modest form gives little reason to expect improvement here.

runners_data.name: Roll It Roisin
runners_data.note: Hold-up type, tongue-tied, who was pulled up on most recent start and finished 7th and 13th in her other two visible runs; only 10 days since last run and no wins or places from two efforts on similar ground — form profile is weak.

runners_data.name: Tiffany Case
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with two runs on Good — a 5th and a 9th — for Sean Flanagan and Barry Connell (0/2 last 14 days); nothing in the profile suggests she can overcome the congested midfield position to land a blow from the back.

runners_data.name: Tutu Twist
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for De Bromhead ridden by O'Keeffe; 142 days off the track is the key query, but she has form on Good and the tongue-tie is retained — sole pace-setter here, which is a major positional asset.

races.paceDynamic: Tutu Twist is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will bowl along at her own tempo through Kilbeggan's 2m3f trip on Good ground — a sustainable, controlled gallop rather than a pressured burn. Through The Storm is the only other horse with prominent leanings and may press into second, but neither horse is likely to force a truly searching pace. The field is loaded with genuine hold-up types — Hey Sir, Kingston Silver, Not In A Hurry, Online Order, Roll It Roisin, Tell Me See, and Tiffany Case all want to come from off the pace — and with the field holding far more hold-up horses than the map can honestly place at the rear, those who cannot get their natural position will race out of role in midfield; of those, Tutu Twist is best placed to control the contest, with Through The Storm the most likely to secure a genuine prominent position behind her. This race shape strongly favours a well-judged prominent or stalking ride, where a horse can travel into a controlled tempo and produce a clean round of jumping, rather than a closer who must find an opening late in a race that may not generate sufficient pace for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tutu Twist Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Tutu Twist jumps cleanly, establishes her lead unchallenged and dictates a measured Good-ground gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Tutu Twist, trained by Henry De Bromhead and ridden by Darragh O'Keeffe, faces no credible pace duel and can regulate every hurdle from the front, arriving at the final flight full of energy. A controlled front-running display on a fair surface suits her profile acutely, and horses forced to race out of their natural hold-up role in the midfield pack will struggle to produce a telling finishing effort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalking Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or close-tracking horse times a smooth move from second or third turning in, jumping better than Tutu Twist late.
scenarios.body: Through The Storm or a lightly-raced unknown type like Blue Trix (W P Mullins) travels prominently within range of the leader and picks her off after the last, benefiting from a gentle gallop that keeps them fresh. This scenario rewards clean jumping and a positive ride rather than any sustained pace test, making the Mullins-Mullins combination on Blue Trix a credible threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens mid-race and the hold-up horses find a clear run around the home bend on the Good surface.
scenarios.body: A genuine closer — Not In A Hurry, who has already placed once, or the experienced Hey Sir — profits if the pace lifts enough to spread the field and create daylight for a late sweeping move. However, with so many horses displaced from their natural hold-up role into midfield, the run of the race may be congested and the probability of a truly clean late passage is lower than the raw numbers suggest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Collapses, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Tutu Twist jumps poorly or fades from the front and the race dissolves into a muddling crawl that nobody controls.
scenarios.body: A disorganised, slow-tempo race opens the door for a lightly-raced or unknown type — The Bossman About or Roll It Roisin — to stumble into contention through attrition as the more fancied runners fail to produce their expected form. This scenario is low probability precisely because the pace picture is clear and Kilbeggan's flat Good ground does not typically generate the chaos needed for rank outsiders to steal the show.

watchPoints.text: Tutu Twist jumping — if she makes an error at any of the early hurdles she loses the lead and her entire race shape unravels, transforming the contest immediately.
Blue Trix on debut — W P Mullins debutants with Danny Mullins up at big fields can arrive fit and ready to win first time; watch the market move as an early guide to the stable's confidence.

Midfield congestion — with at least five genuine hold-up horses crowded into the middle of the pack, there is a meaningful risk of interference or checking on the home turn, affecting the finishing positions of Not In A Hurry, Hey Sir and Online Order simultaneously.

Through The Storm's jumping — this horse's three career starts are all at 2m on softer surfaces; any hesitation at hurdles over an extra three furlongs on Good could see him lose his prominent position to the advantage of Tutu Twist.
Roll It Roisin's fitness — only 10 days since a pulled-up run is a short turnaround; monitor her behaviour in the parade ring for signs of a quick bounce or a purposeful return.

races.name: Clarke's Bar Mullingar Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kamino Bello
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with Gavin Cromwell who handles Good ground well (5 wins or places from 8 similar-going runs) but the 48-day break and a recent form string of 60-60P gives little confidence she finds enough from the rear in a race unlikely to truly test the prominent horses.|

runners_data.name: Imarajan
runners_data.note: Strong course-distance profile with Good-ground form reading 10/14 and a win and two places from five Good-ground runs; Paddy Cody's claim helps with the weight, and the prominent style is perfectly aligned with the likely single-pacemaker shape — this horse is in the right place at the right time.|

runners_data.name: Jacko Star
runners_data.note: 211 days off the track is a major question mark, and the headgear change (hood) suggests connections are hoping for a different response; hold-up style from back of midfield on just 2 from 5 similar-going finishes makes this a speculative reappearance.|

runners_data.name: Rockstown Girl
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner — will lead from flag to finish with no rival threatening to press her — but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.94) reflects that this is effectively a front-runner labelled prominent, and she may fade once the challengers come to her in the straight after dictating throughout.|

runners_data.name: Cocovic
runners_data.note: Ran only 13 days ago and carries headgear (hood); posted two placed efforts from nine Good-ground starts and the hold-up style leaves him reliant on a troubled or faster-than-expected pace to bring him into it.|

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner has run just six days ago, which needs monitoring for freshness, but the prominent style suits the projected race shape perfectly and a record of five places from 15 Good-ground runs shows consistent competitiveness at this level.|

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: Cheekpieces fitted on a hold-up type whose recent form shows back-to-back second places; ran 14 days ago and handles Good ground (7 from 12), but the race shape will require the pace to quicken significantly for him to reach the leaders from off the bridle.|

runners_data.name: Butch Coolidge
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes partnering a horse who won at 22f on Good and has placed on eight of nine similar-going starts — the stay is confirmed; but a hold-up style from the rear means he needs a strong gallop to sustain a run, which the single-pacemaker shape may not provide.|

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Consistent on Good ground (15 from 15 finishes) with a win and six places, and the prominent style is well-suited here; the 7lb claimer Caragh Monaghan needs to use the early rhythm to secure a good position, and the distance is squarely within range.|

runners_data.name: Following Orders
runners_data.note: P J Rothwell runner whose form string of P-09PF is alarming — two pullovers and a fall in recent runs — and the blinkers may be an attempt to sharpen focus; prominent style theoretically suits but jumping reliability is a genuine concern in a field of 17.|

runners_data.name: Premier Rogue
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's five-year-old is a genuine back-of-the-field operator placed in midfield on the map because the field is overloaded with hold-up types; a 95-day absence adds another layer of doubt, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.91) indicates the projected map position is not natural.|

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Cian Collins has a horse in sound form (1W5P from 8 Good-ground runs) with a prominent style that sits cleanly in the projected race shape; ran 13 days ago but remains in form, and the trip at 2m3f is within his range.|

runners_data.name: Smackwater Jack
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old genuine hold-up horse who prefers 24f+ based on recent history — 2m3f is on the short side; the field's volume of back-markers means he is shuffled forward on the map, but that does not reflect his true preference and the STYLE_FIT (0.94) flag confirms the mismatch.|

runners_data.name: Warmer Days Ahead
runners_data.note: 144 days off the track for Oliver McKiernan's seven-year-old, whose last run ended with a pulled-up; a true hold-up operator whose preferred distances trend long, and the lengthy absence combined with the race shape crowding out back-markers makes this a difficult assignment.|

runners_data.name: Bobby Kirova
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with only three career runs who finished third last time — the least experienced runner in the race; a hold-up type whose natural position is compromised by the number of similar operators in the field, and the STYLE_FIT (0.91) tag signals the shown position overstates his likely access to the pace.|

runners_data.name: Tribal
runners_data.note: Shane O'Callaghan's 3lb claimer partners a four-year-old with modest form (best of 5 at 18f Good); hold-up style placed into midfield by redistribution, but this horse has yet to demonstrate the class or the position to challenge in a 17-runner handicap hurdle — STYLE_FIT (0.92) confirms the mismatch.|

runners_data.name: Tudorista
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a critical concern for a hold-up type who needs a strong sustained run home; five from five on Good ground but zero wins and zero places, and the no-jockey-listed entry adds opacity; redistribution into midfield does not change the finishing pattern.|

races.paceDynamic: Rockstown Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-strong field and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, is set to dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m3f at Kilbeggan. The pace is unlikely to be fierce — one horse controlling matters cleanly typically produces a steadily-run race where those tracking the leader closest into the straight hold a decisive positional advantage over true hold-up horses. Prominent-style runners Imarajan, Dairy Force, Sea Of Doubt, Blue Reed, and Following Orders are best placed to exploit this shape, sitting just behind Rockstown Girl and pouncing when she comes off the bridle late. Several horses listed with hold-up styles — Premier Rogue, Smackwater Jack, Warmer Days Ahead, Bobby Kirova, and Tribal — are genuine back-of-the-field types redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains far more hold-up horses than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear, meaning most of them will be further back than ideal and face a stiff task against the pace in a race unlikely to truly fall apart. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel handy without burning energy, as a single-pacemaker scenario at Kilbeggan over this trip historically sees the first two home come from the front four or five.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rockstown Girl Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rockstown Girl leads without challenge and the pace stays measured, allowing prominent trackers to conserve energy for a late surge.
scenarios.body: Rockstown Girl sets an uncontested, controlled tempo and the race develops into a test of class and jumping fluency from the front five; prominent runners travelling sweetly behind her are presented with the perfect opportunity to pounce approaching the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent types positions just off Rockstown Girl's shoulder and produces a clean round of jumping to outstay rivals.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking in second or third throughout gets first run on the field off the final turn, with the steady gallop having preserved enough stamina to sustain the effort to the line; the Good ground and 2m3f trip rewards those who jump well and travel efficiently.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply in the final mile and the prominent horses are caught flat-footed, leaving a gap for midfield types to come through.
scenarios.body: A scenario requiring the gallop to genuinely test the prominent horses earlier than expected, creating a strong late run from the chasing pack; however, several of the nominal midfield runners are redistributed hold-up types racing somewhat out of their ideal role, limiting the depth of the late charge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If a cluster of early fallers, bunching at hurdles, or a dramatic acceleration breaks the race into fragments with no clear positional advantage.
scenarios.body: A messy, stop-start gallop could strip away Rockstown Girl's lead advantage and hand the initiative to whoever picks the best ground through the field; even in this scenario the true hold-up horses face the longest journey and the race still most likely resolves in favour of a horse that had been travelling in the first half of the field.

watchPoints.text: Rockstown Girl's jumping must be monitored — if she makes a significant error early she will lose her unpressured lead and the entire race shape collapses, leaving prominent trackers like Imarajan and Dairy Force suddenly involved in a scramble for position.|

Following Orders has fallen, unseated, and pulled up in three of six recent runs — with 17 runners over hurdles on a flat Kilbeggan track, a jumping incident from this horse could cause interference to any runner tracking close to the inside.|

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Premier Rogue, Smackwater Jack, Warmer Days Ahead, Bobby Kirova, Tribal) will be jostling for the same patch of ground in the first half of the field; watch for crowding at the early flights that could check multiple runners simultaneously.|

Dairy Force ran only six days ago — if the Gordon Elliott runner travels strongly early but weakens sharply after the last, recency fatigue rather than lack of class may be the explanation, and that signals a pace collapse that could favour a late mover like Cocovic or Butch Coolidge.|
